A post-void residual of 25 mL indicates only a mild retention, which is unlikely to be the sole cause of your severe discomfort. Have you experienced any urgency, incontinence, or a sensation of incomplete bladder emptying?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Cystoscopy: Normal urethra and bladder mucosa; Pelvic Ultrasound (Bladder): Postvoid Residual Urine 25 mL

speaker: Doctor
text: The cystoscopy and ultrasound results are reassuring, showing no structural abnormalities or significant retention. Since your initial infection workup was negative and there are no visible obstructions, have you noticed any relief of your symptoms during or after bowel movements?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: The fact that your bladder discomfort is relieved by voiding, along with dyspareunia (painful intercourse) and a negative workup for infection or structural issues, is highly suggestive of a specific pelvic floor condition. Do you experience pelvic pain or pressure that improves after passing urine?

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on your symptoms of chronic pelvic pain relieved by voiding, urinary frequency, and dyspareunia, combined with negative infectious and structural workups, these findings are highly characteristic of Interstitial Cystitis (Painful Bladder Syndrome). Do you have any known allergies to food additives like benzoates or sulfites?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis (Painful Bladder Syndrome)
